findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that `_display_path` compares against a resolved REPO_ROOT (e.g. `REPO_ROOT.resolve()`), so in-repo files never take the absolute-path fallback.
evidence: "`path.resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()`, falling back to `path.resolve().as_posix()` on `ValueError` for a file outside the repo"
findings.finding: `_display_path` computes `path.resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT)`. If REPO_ROOT is not itself resolved, then for a checkout reached through a symlink or alias the resolved file path no longer has REPO_ROOT as a prefix. Examples are macOS `/tmp` → `/private/tmp`, symlinked workspace dirs, and Windows 8.3 short names such as `RUNNER~1`, which `resolve()` expands. In that case `relative_to` raises ValueError for in-repo files and the helper silently falls back to absolute paths. The plan does not state that REPO_ROOT is resolved, and that fact is load-bearing.
findings.location: Approach — (1, 2) `_display_path` helper
scenarios: macOS developer workstation with the checkout under a symlinked path: every FAIL line and GitHub annotation names an absolute path instead of `skills/…/SKILL.md`.
Windows CI runner whose checkout path contains an 8.3 short name: annotations carry absolute paths and do not attach to files.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `path.resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT.resolve()).as_posix()` (or assert REPO_ROOT is defined via `Path(__file__).resolve()`).
